title: Pressure and hydrostatics; Upthrust / Archimedes' principle
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: FL02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; FL02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; FL02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; FL03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: FL02-1#N.2, FL03-1#N.4b, FL02-1#N.3, FL03-1#N.7, FL02-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Incompressible
items.clue: Describes a liquid whose ρ is the same at every depth.

items.label: Pascal
items.clue: Unit equal to 1 N m⁻², that is, one newton on each square m.

items.label: Pressure
items.clue: Total perpendicular force divided by area; exists at every place in a gas.

items.label: Archimedes' principle
items.clue: Statement that the upward push from a fluid equals the weight of fluid displaced.

questions.stem: A force of 50 N acts on a flat plate of area 25 cm². The force is at 60° to the plate's surface. What pressure does the force exert on the plate?
questions.explanation: The angle is from the surface, so the perpendicular component is 50 sin 60° = 43.3 N. A = 25 × 10⁻⁴ m², so pressure = 43.3 ÷ 2.5 × 10⁻³ = 1.7 × 10⁴ Pa.

questions.stem: Two solid balls of equal volume, one made of lead and one of aluminum, hang from strings so that each is completely under water at the same depth. Lead is denser than aluminum. How does the buoyant force on the lead ball compare with the buoyant force on the aluminum ball?

options.text: Greater on the lead ball, since it has the greater mass
Greater on the aluminum ball, since it is the less dense
Zero on both, since both would sink if released
Equal, since the balls displace equal volumes of water

questions.stem: A sealed container holds a gas at a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa. Which statement about this pressure is correct?

options.text: The gas presses mainly on the base of the container, because gas pressure acts downwards.
Pressure is a vector, so the pressures acting on opposite walls of the container cancel out.
The gas exerts a force of 1.0 × 10⁵ N on each wall, whatever the area of that wall.
The gas pushes perpendicular to every wall, exerting 1.0 × 10⁵ N on each square metre of wall.

questions.stem: A foam ball of volume V would float, but it is held at rest completely under water by a light string tied to the bottom of a tank. The density of the foam is a quarter of the density ρ of water. Which expression gives the tension in the string?
